title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for intent→configuration artifacts produced by a declared/requested model ("gpt-5-mini", provider: openai_responses). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and a preregistered paired design (Npairs = 720), the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111 and the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded outcomes lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, an explicit explanation of provider-call accounting, and an artifact-grounded interpretation: in this curated regime a strong static validator produced a ceiling effect that left essentially no headroom for guarded sandboxing to add aggregate detection coverage. We identify boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter and point to the archived execution bundle for independent verification.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational use requires generated artifacts to satisfy parser-level syntax, workflow-order constraints, invariants (e.g., at‑least‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute; researchers also propose adding sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports document this pattern but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution. Motivated by this gap, we preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that isolates downstream guarded-stage effects by reusing the identical sampled candidate across both conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Our contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting; (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation explaining a near-zero marginal effect in this regime; (4) prescriptive boundary conditions and reproducibility pointers to the archived bundle.
sections.related_work: Tooling and workflow-centered evaluations emphasize pairing LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance for intent→configuration pipelines [1]. Work on configuration-analysis tools documents evolving rule-sets and topology-aware static checks but highlights coverage gaps for runtime-dependent and stateful sequences; that motivates emulator-assisted validation as a practical mitigation [2]. Prototype and empirical reports across NetOps and code/specification domains show heterogeneous gains from guarded pipelines: emulation detects runtime semantics and side-effects in some regimes but yields little marginal benefit when static validators already align tightly with the task distribution [3]. These findings justify a paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate solely downstream guarded-stage contributions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Planned Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440), minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 for power planning. Inclusion/exclusion, missingness, multiplicity, contamination, and repair policies were frozen in the preregistration.

Task bank and generation semantics. Confirmatory items were produced deterministically from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 generator covering three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; the run produced zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720. Shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: for each pair exactly one sampled initial candidate was produced and that identical candidate was evaluated under both (baseline) validator-only and (guarded) validator+emulation conditions. This isolates any between-condition discordance to downstream validation, emulation observations, or permitted repair.

Model, validator, and guarded harness. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses). Baseline validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 — a deterministic rule-based checker that performs vendor-CLI parsing, canonicalization, command-sequence and workflow-order checks (make-before-break, all_down_before_any_field_change, protected-interface invariants), group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then (irrespective of validator outcome) executes the candidate in a sandboxed emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology template and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices; emulation produces runtime observations translated to runtime-observation rules that can trigger detections not captured by static rules.

Provider-call accounting: meaning of audit fields. The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation include a provider_call_audit object with counts such as hosted_model_call_event_count and stage_counts (shared_initial_generation, repair) and condition_counts (shared, guarded). Explanation: 'shared' in the audit refers to the shared initial-generation calls that produced the single sampled candidate reused across the paired conditions (one per pair). 'Guarded' entries in condition_counts indicate calls that occurred exclusively inside the guarded pipeline (for example, a repair-stage model invocation that is not part of the shared initial generation). Stage_counts enumerate logical execution stages and their call counts (the confirmatory run shows shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1). Thus model_calls_used = 721 corresponds to 720 shared initial calls plus one additional repair-stage call recorded only in the guarded stage; this accounting is archived in the deterministic_reconciliation artifacts and in provider_call_audit.

Analysis plan and executors. The primary analysis is a paired-binary procedure (McNemar-style exact test) with paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) as preregistered. The primary analysis excluded irrecoverable technical pairs per preregistration; in the confirmatory run no such exclusions occurred. All analysis code and raw artifacts used as inputs are archived and cited in the reproducibility pointers below.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 720. Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1). All numeric values are reproduced verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts.

Discordant-pair attribution (artifact-grounded). Deterministic reconciliation and the raw_results archive link the single n10 discordant episode to the lone repair-stage call: the archived raw_results.jsonl record for that pair contains a non-null repair_provider_trace field (and pair_id) that corresponds to the single repair invocation recorded in provider_call_audit. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the possible proximate causes for that discordant detection are limited to (i) the recorded repair-stage invocation altering the candidate accepted by the guarded scorer or (ii) an emulation-observed runtime violation not codified in the static validator; the archived per-episode artifacts permit independent inspection of validator_trace and repair_provider_trace to determine which occurred for that pair.
sections.discussion:
Why the guarded-stage aggregate benefit was negligible. Three artifact-grounded factors explain the near-zero paired difference in this run. (1) Validator ceiling effect: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encoded the syntactic and workflow checks emphasized by the deterministic task generator; representative validator_trace objects in execution/scoring show parsed_command_count and required_command_count equal and violation_count = 0 for most shared_initial candidates, producing baseline coverage of 719/720. (2) Curated inclusion reduces adversarial exposure: inclusion required parser acceptance and deterministic generation, concentrating confirmatory items in regions where the validator already matches task patterns. (3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and minimal repair activity: reuse of the identical sampled candidate for both conditions isolates downstream effects and the run recorded only one repair-stage call (repair = 1), which corresponds to the unique n10 episode.

Operational implications and boundary conditions. The evidence implies a conditional efficiency boundary: when operator pipelines enforce tight prevalidation and a high-coverage static validator is deployed, automated sandboxed emulation may yield negligible marginal detection gains at scale. This does not generalize broadly. Guarded stages are more likely to add value in regimes with (a) noisy or unconstrained natural-language intents, (b) adversarially crafted misconfigurations, (c) richer vendor-CLI diversity that challenges parser/validator coverage, or (d) long-lived stateful interactions requiring higher-fidelity emulation. The archived artifacts provide concrete seed traces to construct adversarial test banks and to retest guarded pipelines under expanded distributions.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator and the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated, parser-validated synthetic task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; archived artifacts permit independent verification of that mapping. We interpret the near-zero aggregate effect as the consequence of validator ceiling effects in a tightly curated regime and recommend focused follow-ups using adversarial tasks, expanded vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive operational value. Reproducibility pointers: canonical artifacts and analysis outputs cited below enable independent auditing.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
